subject: Referral from systems validation team - Encord ML DataOps
text:
Hey [NAME],

Been chatting to some of your [COMPANY] colleagues across the systems
validation, LiDAR eng, AI eng and functional owner teams about the CV
DataOps pipelines at [COMPANY] and I was pointed in your direction for
evaluation.

From our conversations there were some common themes popping up around data
management pains. The key areas we support is around:

   - Making better use of existing camera datasets across programs, rather
   than re-collecting or re-annotating for each new customer or geography
   - Active learning - so finding and prioritising the specific scenes and
   edge cases that actually drive model improvements
   - Reducing the cost and effort of annotation and review which is
   currently significant

For a bit of context we are supporting ADAS teams like Woven-Toyota with
these exact problems at the moment.

Would you have some in the next few weeks to explore where we could
potentially help and explore wether there is any fit?

subject: Web Agent Trajectory Evals
text:
Hi [NAME],

I saw the recent after_date filter added to Parallel's Search API, a solid
improvement for agent workflows where freshness impacts downstream
reasoning and task success.

We've been working with Yutori on web agent trajectory evaluation,
capturing full end-to-end runs (search, navigation, tool calls) and running
repeatable, head-to-head evals to quantify regressions and improvements as
web systems change.

Given Parallel's focus on agent-friendly search and verification, I thought
this might be relevant to what you're building.

Case study for context:

[LINK]

Would you or someone on your team be open to connecting?

subject: Human in the loop web grading
text:
Hi [NAME],

I read about [COMPANY]'s approach to evals which focuses on grading retrieval and
downstream task utility using open evals and LLM graders.

LLM graders are good at does this look right, but have trouble with:
- Did it complete the task but inefficiently
- Did it solve the task with an incorrect assumption
- Did the agent get 2/3 tasks correct

We've been working with Yutori on capturing full end-to-end runs and
scoring them with structured failure taxonomies so improvements are
measurable.

Case study here:
[LINK]

It's an evolving process on our side, would you or someone on your team be
open to connect briefly?
